briefing.opening: Good day. Welcome to the Climate Daily Briefing for November 12, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 2.7°C Warming Warning and Stalled COP31 Summit Negotiations
sections.content: A grave analysis has warned that if current national policies remain in place, global average temperatures could rise by 2.7°C by the end of this century, irreversibly breaching the 1.5°C threshold [17, 21, 167]. At the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) held in Antalya, Türkiye, criticism has intensified over the stagnation of global climate action over the past five years [21, 136, 142]. With a leadership void emerging from the absence of heads of state from major emitting nations, concerns are growing over weakening momentum for international cooperation [9, 140], while leaders of climate-vulnerable countries are warning of planetary ecosystem collapse and pleading for bold emissions cuts and immediate action from member states [144, 160].

sections.title: ⚠️ Expanding Antarctic Ozone Hole to Drought: Escalating Climate Disasters
sections.content: The Antarctic ozone hole, which had previously shown signs of shrinking, has expanded to a massive size once again due to recent extreme weather events, heightening environmental alarm [23]. Domestically, while the government officially issued drought forecasts and advisories for November, concerns were raised that investments in climate disaster prevention remain sidelined compared to renewable energy [8, 11]. Meanwhile, around the globe, dawn glacial floods, record-high coastal water temperatures in California, and rapid shifts in storm patterns were reported [19, 110], with escalating extreme weather exacerbating future food security risks and deepening climate anxiety among younger generations [148, 165].

sections.title: 🌍 Massive Clean Energy Investments and Global Mitigation Cooperation Spurred by COP31
sections.content: COP31 host nation Türkiye signed a record $1.6 billion climate policy agreement with the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and concluded a preliminary deal to secure a $15 billion investment from China for solar and wind energy projects [121, 170]. At the summit, discussions focused in depth on industrial electrification alongside grid modernization and energy storage system (ESS) expansion, as well as the '35 by 35' electricity expansion target [2, 6]. International solidarity is also actively expanding, with K-water agreeing to cooperate with Liverpool, UK on tidal power generation, and South Korea and Japan jointly exploring energy security and carbon neutrality in Osaka [35, 44].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Large-Scale Offshore Wind Groundbreaking and Future Climate-Resilient Agricultural Innovations
sections.content: Domestically, POSCO E&C has broken ground on the 297.4 billion KRW Gochang Offshore Wind Farm (76.2 MW) in North Jeolla Province to provide a stable supply of renewable energy to high-tech industries in the southwestern region [86, 92, 96]. Ulsan Metropolitan City officially submitted a proposal to the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment urging the accelerated implementation of floating offshore wind projects to resolve power supply issues for key industries and expedite the energy transition [61, 105]. Concurrently, in the agricultural sector, climate adaptation technology innovations are accelerating, with Haenam County presenting a vision for advanced climate-resilient agriculture and a Kyung Hee University research team securing an AI-driven 'multidimensional root rice design' research center [1, 3, 26].

briefing.closing: That concludes today's climate briefing. We will continue to closely monitor global resolve and action to prevent crossing critical temperature thresholds.
